title: Work2Skill: Capturing Human GUI Experience for Reusable Agent Skill Induction
excerpt: Computer-use agents can perform increasingly complex GUI tasks, yet unfamiliar software and workflows requiring human domain knowledge remain challenging. Human demonstrations convey procedural knowledge through the same GUI interaction space, but reuse requires interpreting actions in context and separating workflow rules from task-specific details. We thus introduce Work2Skill, a framework that captures human GUI experience for reusable agent skill induction. WorkRecorder provides the framework's infrastructure for collecting this experience, aligning screen recordings, mouse and keyboard events, and available accessibility-tree information. Using WorkRecorder, we construct WorkDemo-350…

ai.summary: Work2Skill introduces a framework that records human interactions with GUIs and extracts reusable skills for agents, separating workflow rules from task‑specific details.
ai.why: Developers can leverage the captured skills to quickly teach agents new software tasks without extensive retraining.

title: RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models
excerpt: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) aims to transform interaction experience into persistent improvements, yet external feedback is costly and world-model predictions may become unreliable as policies evolve. We introduce RSI-Anything, a domain-general framework built on JEPA-Anything that uses predictive world models to guide action and learning-data selection. Observed feedback drives policy or workflow improvement and conditional world-model adaptation, while component and compatibility checks govern the retention of updated policy-model pairs. title: Reflex: Visually Grounded Reactive Humanoid Control
excerpt: Humans effortlessly react to the world; they adeptly return a tennis shot, catch a falling cup, step aside from a passing cart, or pass a box tossed during truck unloading. These everyday actions require anticipating a moving target and reflexively responding with the whole body within about a second. Such visual reactive whole-body control remains challenging for humanoids, which must (1) coordinate whole-body control, (2) react to object dynamics in real time, and (3) ground perception in egocentric vision. We study catching thrown boxes as a representative task that demands all three capabilities; existing systems cover only part of it, relying on end-effectors, motion capture, or marked…

ai.summary: The paper introduces Reflex, a system for visually grounded reactive whole‑body control of humanoid robots that can anticipate moving targets and respond within about one second.
ai.why: Enables developers to build robots that react to dynamic environments in real time, advancing manipulation and navigation tasks.

title: Inducing Process Supervision from Outcome-Only Reinforcement Learning
excerpt: Process reward models (PRMs) have become a key component for LLMs, as their step-level feedback supports both post-training and test-time reasoning. However, training strong PRMs remains costly: human step annotation is difficult to scale, while Monte Carlo estimation is computationally expensive and can drift from the intrinsic correctness of steps. To get effective PRMs at low cost, we introduce TIPS (Thinking-Induced Process Supervision), an outcome-only reinforcement learning (RL) framework for training generative PRMs. In TIPS, the model generates a chain-of-thought (CoT) followed by step-level labels and an outcome label. The reward depends solely on whether the predicted outcome…

ai.summary: TIPS (Thinking‑Induced Process Supervision) is an outcome‑only RL framework that generates process reward models for LLMs without step‑level human annotations.
ai.why: Allows developers to cheaply train step‑wise reward models for LLMs, improving reasoning and alignment with less annotation cost.

title: SoloQ: Calibration-Free Quantization for Diffusion Language Models
excerpt: Diffusion large language models dLLMs) have emerged as a promising alternative to autoregressive language models through bidirectional diffusion-based token generation. However, their growing model sizes and high inference costs make efficient deployment challenging: full-sequence denoising repeatedly invokes compute-intensive forward passes, while block-diffusion models additionally introduce a memory-intensive KV-cache. Low-bit weight-activation quantization is therefore attractive, yet existing dLLM post-training quantization methods rely on calibration data despite activation distributions shifting across masking states and denoising steps. ai.summary: SoloQ introduces a calibration‑free quantization technique for diffusion language models that reduces weight and activation precision without requiring post‑hoc calibration, aiming to cut inference cost and memory usage.
ai.why: Allows developers to deploy large diffusion‑based LLMs more efficiently on limited hardware.

title: DiffusionART: Efficient, Stable and Scalable Reinforcement of Diffusion Models
excerpt: Online reinforcement learning (RL) fine-tunes diffusion models with black-box rewards, but reverse-process methods such as Flow-GRPO are limited in efficiency by poor credit assignment, while forward-process methods such as DiffusionNFT are efficient yet unstable without carefully tuned exponential-moving-average (EMA) off-policy training. We show that NFT-style objectives contain a hidden forward--reverse consistency force that joint positive--negative training cancels only partially, and that EMA stabilizes training through restoration rather than off-policy rollouts. We introduce DiffusionART (Diffusion Reinforcement with Aggregation-First Reward Tilting), which aggregates each prompt's…

ai.summary: DiffusionART introduces a reinforcement learning method for diffusion models that combines forward‑process and reverse‑process objectives to achieve stable and efficient fine‑tuning with black‑box rewards.

In this paper, we evaluate the performance of LLMs for two prominent MT quality evaluation schemes: Multidimensional Quality Metrics (MQM) and Error Span Annotation (ESA) by comparing their agreement with human…

title: Self-Compacting Language Model Agents
excerpt: Long agent traces composed of chains of thought and tool calls accumulate stale content that anchor subsequent generations, and eventually outgrow the context window. Existing scaffolds mitigate it with fixed-interval compaction triggered at a token threshold. Such triggers pay no heed to trajectory structure, risking discard of partial results mid-derivation or mid-search. We propose SELFCOMPACT, a scaffold that allows the model itself to decide when and how to compact. ai.summary: Apple ML researchers propose SELFCOMPACT, a mechanism that lets language model agents decide when to compress their internal reasoning traces, reducing context window overflow and stale information.

excerpt: Recent joint video-audio generation models have achieved strong semantic correspondence and temporal synchronization. We refer to this property as Dynamic Spatial Correspondence and propose StereoBind, a framework that binds visual source motion to stereo sound generation. excerpt: Continual learning requires models to accumulate past experience and transfer it to new tasks. To address this gap, we introduce EmbodiedCLBench, the first benchmark in embodied simulation for evaluating the continual learning capability of self-evolving agents. With compositional generalization as the core evaluation principle, our benchmark evaluates whether agents can first learn from basic tasks and then recombine the acquired skills to solve complex, unseen advanced tasks. Based on EmbodiedCLBench, we conduct extensive…

title: Learning Representations to Guide Pixel Diffusion Transformers
excerpt: Visual representations are largely developed for understanding, yet what makes them useful for generation remains unclear. We study this question in pixel diffusion transformers and uncover two key insights. First, better representation quality does not necessarily translate into greater generative utility, as externally aligned semantics can be progressively lost during pixel synthesis. Second, architectural separation with specialized pixel decoders mainly redistributes semantic and spatial modeling, without necessarily yielding representations better suited to generation. These insights suggest that a useful generative representation must be both properly formed and actively exploited…

ai.summary: The authors analyze pixel diffusion transformers and find that higher‑quality visual representations do not always improve generation, and that separating pixel decoders reallocates semantic and spatial information.

title: SepGen: Multi-Stem Audio-Video Separation and Generation in a Single Model
excerpt: A 4D audio-visual scene comprises a video, the dynamic geometry it depicts, and the sound sources that populate it, each with its own position and trajectory. Joint audio-video generators can synthesize the video and its soundtrack, but the soundtrack is emitted as a single audio-mix in which the sources are not individually accessible. title: S-Space: Exploring Spatial Workspace in Multimodal Language Models
excerpt: Multimodal language models (MLLMs) exhibit promising spatial reasoning capabilities, yet the internal mechanisms supporting them remain poorly understood. We uncover S-Space, a linear representation subspace in which object-token representations encode continuous coordinates along horizontal, vertical, and distance axes. Although we identify these axes by differentiating spatial-answer scores with respect to object-token activations, S-Space is intrinsic rather than induced by specific data or prompts, remaining readable under non-spatial questions. ai.summary: The paper “S‑Space” shows that multimodal language models contain a linear subspace where object‑token activations encode continuous horizontal, vertical, and distance coordinates, revealing intrinsic spatial reasoning mechanisms.

excerpt: Continual post-training faces a dual challenge of acquisition and retention: models must learn new capabilities while preserving prior knowledge. excerpt: Multimodal large language models have become the dominant paradigm for visual understanding, but incur substantial costs by encoding inputs into dense, fixed-size patch tokens. title: Hello Python 3.15, goodbye 3.10, and now I can use 3.11

First, some highlights from Python 3.15.
Explicit lazy imports
I'm most excited about Explicit lazy imports from PEP 810 . These let you import modules like so:
lazy import json
lazy from pathlib import Path
The module will then be imported the first time those symbols are used in the code that follows.
